gap: No result ChatGPT got says how bright each bundle's projector makes its own included screen in foot-lamberts: the Fugoo kit ChatGPT kept recommending lights its 120-in screen to about 5.9 ft-L, roughly a third of the 16 ft-L dark-room target, which suits a picture of about 73 in. The JMGO PicoPlay+ gives about 15.2 ft-L on its 100-in screen, close to the target.
standout_why: Our own page (dealectric.com/best-portable-projector-with-screen) already uses ft-L, but only for the Aurzen D1/D1 MAX, Yaber and TMY. It covers none of the bundles ChatGPT actually showed (Fugoo, JMGO PicoPlay+ Costco, Vankyo H500RS, ETOE Seal Pro 120-in). The RTINGS page came back to WebFetch as navigation only, with no spec or brightness text. On it and on the Woot, ProjectorCentral and Notebookcheck pages I opened, nothing turns lumens into on-screen brightness for a bundled screen. I did not open TechRadar, Crutchfield or What Hi-Fi within the budget, so I can't rule out that they discuss it, though ChatGPT's answers never mention screen brightness. The new part is applying ft-L to the specific kits shoppers are shown, and the result that two of them (Fugoo, Vankyo) ship a screen bigger than their projector can light properly.
decides: It changes the pick. The cheap kits ChatGPT leads with (Fugoo $149.99, and our own Aurzen D1 + 120-in screen at 5.15 ft-L) only reach the 16 ft-L dark-room target at about 68 to 73 in, so their 120-in screens are mostly for show. The Vankyo H500R is rated by its maker for up to 80 in, yet the H500RS bundle comes with a 100-in screen (11.1 ft-L). The JMGO PicoPlay+ (450 ISO lm, 100-in screen, 15.2 ft-L, 3 h battery) is the only bundle shown that fills its own screen at the target and also runs one full film without a wall plug. The ETOE Seal Pro (23.4 ft-L at 120 in) and our Aurzen D1 MAX (25.7 ft-L at 120 in, gain 1.1) are the plug-in picks for a full 120-in screen. The Seal Pro draws 180 W and weighs 10.4 lb, so it is only nominally portable.

findings.label: Dark-room brightness target and formula
findings.value: 16 ft-L; ft-L = lumens × gain / screen sq ft
findings.source_title: ProjectorCentral: Simple Guide to Calculating Projector Lumens
findings.note: Quote: 'the most common brightness recommendation is 16 foot-lamberts (ft-L)'; formula quoted as 'ft-L = Lumens X Gain / SquareFeet'. 16:9 screen area in sq ft = diagonal² × 0.0029674, so 120 in = 42.73 sq ft, 100 in = 29.67 sq ft.

findings.label: Projector brightness and screen included
findings.value: 250 ANSI lm; 120-in screen; $129.99 at Woot, sold out
findings.note: Woot gives no offer date and the listing is sold out. Includes the 1080p projector, a 20 W soundbar, a 120-in screen and cables; the features text also mentions a 35-in tripod. Screen gain is not published.

findings.label: Brightness on its own 120-in screen (gain 1.0 assumed)
findings.value: 5.85 ft-L (37% of 16 ft-L); suits up to about 73 in at 16 ft-L
findings.note: 250 / 42.73 = 5.85 ft-L; largest image at 16 ft-L: √((250/16)/0.0029674) = √5266 = 72.6 in. This is an upper bound because it ignores lens and keystone losses.

findings.label: Brightness, power, battery, weight, MSRP
findings.value: 450 ISO lm (ISO 21118); 65 W; 3 h battery life; 2.2 lb; $499 MSRP
findings.note: The spec page says 'A detachable battery base provides cordless flexibility.' The Costco bundle's 100-in screen size comes from the Costco listing title in ChatGPT's results. The Costco page itself returned HTTP 429.

findings.label: Brightness on its own 100-in screen (gain 1.0 assumed)
findings.value: 15.2 ft-L (95% of 16 ft-L); suits up to about 97 in at 16 ft-L
findings.note: 450 / 29.67 = 15.17 ft-L; √((450/16)/0.0029674) = √9478 = 97.4 in. ISO lumens are not identical to ANSI lumens.

findings.label: Films per charge (2-hour film)
findings.note: 3 h ÷ 2 h = 1.5. Uses the listed 3-hour battery life; brightness mode is not stated.
